text:
Omar El-Sayed: Heads up — I think we found the root cause of the SCM mismatch on `batch_size_effective`. We’re currently computing it *pre* admission-control (i.e., before we drop/reshape batches under load), so the signal is inflated when the scheduler is shedding.

Omar El-Sayed: Example from staging under synthetic load:
- runtime emits `batch_size_effective=16` for decode step
- actual admitted decode microbatches are ~8–10
This lines up w/ the drift alerts Rafael’s canary flagged yesterday.

Omar El-Sayed: I put up a fix in PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18618
TL;DR: move `batch_size_effective` to be derived from post-admission batch metadata (after token budget + queue gate), and add a regression test that compares emitted metric vs scheduler’s admitted batch size.

Omar El-Sayed: Can someone sanity-check perf impact? This is on the hot path and I’d rather not regress p95 decode latency for the sake of a metric.

Sofia Ivanova: :eyes: thanks. This explains why the metric looked “too good to be true” when we enabled the new admission policy.

Sofia Ivanova: Looking at the diff now — are we adding any extra locks / atomics in decode loop?

Omar El-Sayed: No new locks. Previously we were reading `planned_batch_size` from the request group before scheduler finalize.
Now we read `admitted_batch_size` that’s already computed during finalize; it’s a field on the batch struct. One extra pointer deref, but same callsite.

Jordan Lee: From the SCM side this is the right behavior. Determinism/attribution assumes `batch_size_effective` reflects *actual work done* not intended work.

Jordan Lee: Also +1 on the regression test; we should catch this class of “computed pre-gate” bug for other signals too.

Rafael Mendes: This matches what perf-canary is seeing. The drift detector trips specifically when `admission_control=on` and queue depth > ~200.

Rafael Mendes: For perf regression check: want me to run the standard runtime perf suite on the PR commit? (A10 + H100 configs)

Mateo Alvarez: Yes please. Let’s not merge until we’re confident overhead is basically noise.

Mateo Alvarez: @Omar El-Sayed can you paste the benchmark command you used locally (if any) so Rafael runs the same thing?

Omar El-Sayed: Sure — locally I ran:
```
./bazel run //runtime/perf:decode_bench -- \
  --model=llama-70b \
  --seq_in=256 --seq_out=256 \
  --concurrency=64 \
  --admission_control=on \
  --duration_s=180
```
And compared HEAD vs PR branch, same GPU + driver.

Omar El-Sayed: Local results on H100 were within run-to-run variance (~0.2–0.4%). But I didn’t do a full matrix.

Sean Gallagher: :wave: SRE side: if this touches counters only, shouldn’t impact latency. But we’ve been burned by “harmless metrics” before.

Sean Gallagher: Please capture p95/p99 decode + CPU overhead in the report. If anything >1% we should treat as suspect.

Sofia Ivanova: I see we also changed where we increment the per-step counter. That could affect ordering of writes to the metrics buffer, but shouldn’t be measurable.

Sofia Ivanova: One thing: ensure it’s still emitted when `admission_control=off` (i.e., batch struct is always populated). Looks like yes.

Omar El-Sayed: Yep — when admission is off, admitted==planned. The struct exists in both paths.

Rafael Mendes: Kicking off perf suite now. Will post numbers here when done. :runner:

Rafael Mendes: Results (staging perf runner, H100, same workload as Omar command + a couple extra):
- decode p95 latency: +0.06%
- decode p99 latency: -0.11%
- throughput tokens/s: +0.03%
- CPU util: +0.2pp (within noise)
- scheduler finalize time: no change
Looks clean.

Mateo Alvarez: Great. :thumbsup: from me.

Sofia Ivanova: +1, looks safe. Thanks for catching this.

Jordan Lee: Once merged, can we make sure the SCM service notes mention this metric semantic? (post-admission) It’ll matter for explain payloads.

Omar El-Sayed: Yep, I’ll add a short note in the runtime signals doc / follow-up PR. Merging after CI finishes.
